title: MergeSemantics drops descendant semantics
evidence: Revalidated at a19bf487: semantics__merge diverges at frame 1 (16 ms). Flutter exposes one node labelled North and South (11 characters); Incular has zero nodes. Incular semantic_children returns no children for a merge_descendants widget (tree/semantics.rs:263), and no aggregate node is built for the wrapper.
impact: A group of controls placed under MergeSemantics can disappear from the accessibility tree, so no spoken label or actionable control is exposed for it.
cause: Incular treats merge as do not traverse descendants, and does not aggregate descendant labels, roles, states or actions onto the wrapper.
fix_direction: Build one semantic node for the merging wrapper from its descendants, following Flutter's label joining with newlines and its rules for merged roles, state and actions.
limitations: Only the label count and length were sampled; role, state and action aggregation were not compared.

title: Unspecified enabled state is projected as disabled
evidence: Revalidated at a19bf487: semantics__enabled_default diverges at frame 1. Flutter enabled is Tristate.none (2); Incular stores false (0). Both expose Button label Action with a tap action. accessibility lib.rs:805 sets disabled for an interactive role whenever state.enabled is false.
impact: An application that leaves enabled unspecified, as Flutter allows, can expose an actionable Incular button to AccessKit as disabled.
cause: SemanticState::enabled is a plain bool whose default is false, so unspecified and explicitly disabled are the same state.
fix_direction: Represent the unspecified state separately (for example Option<bool>) and set disabled only for an explicit false.
limitations: Checked through the retained tree and the AccessKit source; native assistive technology was not run.

title: Scroll actions remain advertised at exhausted edges
evidence: Revalidated at a19bf487: Horizontal axis (semantics__horizontal_scroll, added at resume) shows the same pattern: frame 1 Flutter scrollLeft+scrollRight count 1, Incular 2; position and maximum extent match. scroll position 0, maximum extent 600 and child count 12 match. At frame 1 Flutter advertises one direction (scroll_up 1, scroll_down 0) while Incular advertises both. At frame 3, after jumping to maximum, Flutter has scroll_up 0 and scroll_down 1 while Incular still has scroll_up 1.
impact: Assistive technology offers a scroll direction that cannot move the list at that boundary.
cause: The scroll node's action list is fixed to ScrollForward and ScrollBackward (tree/semantics.rs:740-756) and is not recomputed from the controller offset and extents.
fix_direction: Recompute the advertised scroll actions when offset or extent changes, using Flutter's axis-aware forward and backward mapping.
limitations: Only the vertical list is scenario-checked. Horizontal axes were not compared.

title: Label-only Semantics without a role or action is dropped
evidence: New at a19bf487: a container Semantics with label Label only and no role, action or flag produces one Flutter node and zero Incular nodes. Explicit descriptors require a role (semantics.rs:364), and the semantics pass emits a node only when a role is derived (tree/semantics.rs:818). The label is kept in semantic_properties but is used only by a node that already has a role. The sibling labelled Plain matches because on_tap assigns Button (see semantics-005).
impact: Labelled containers that carry no control role, such as a labelled region or a summary, are absent from the accessibility tree.
cause: The node-creation rule requires a role, and the label fallback is applied only inside roled nodes.
fix_direction: Emit a generic container node for a Semantics wrapper that has a label, value, description, flag or action, and keep Flutter's container semantics for when that node is created.
limitations: Only the label and absence of a node were sampled. Flutter's non-container merge into an ancestor was not compared; see semantics-012.
verified_by: orchestrator package rerun (scenario-backed) or independent source verification (source-only); see VERIFICATION.md and verification-source-findings.md

title: onTap and onIncrease imply Button and Slider roles
evidence: New at a19bf487: a container Semantics with label Plain and onTap has no button flag in Flutter, while Incular reports Role::Button. on_tap calls role.get_or_insert(Button) and on_increase calls get_or_insert(Slider), so the role is set implicitly.
impact: Screen readers announce a control type the app never declared, for example button for a plain tappable region, and the role changes if the app later sets an explicit role.
cause: The builder fills in a control role as a side effect of setting a callback.
fix_direction: Keep callbacks separate from role. Attach the tap or increase action without changing the role, and let the app specify the role.
limitations: Flutter's onIncrease with a slider flag was not compared. The role difference was checked for onTap only.
verified_by: orchestrator package rerun (scenario-backed) or independent source verification (source-only); see VERIFICATION.md and verification-source-findings.md

title: Hint and tooltip share one description field, and state.tooltip is never set
evidence: New at a19bf487: a node with hint Adjusts volume and tooltip Volume has Flutter hint length 14 and tooltip length 6. Incular stores only one string: the description is Volume (length 6), since tooltip overwrites hint (both builders write description, semantics.rs:119-131). The tooltip field of SemanticState (the one accessibility uses at lib.rs:836) is never set, so its length is 0 against Flutter 6.
impact: A hint is lost whenever a tooltip is also given, and the tooltip is exposed as a description rather than a tooltip property.
cause: hint(), tooltip() and accessibility_description() all write the same description field, and the Semantics builder never writes state.tooltip.
fix_direction: Store hint, tooltip and description as separate fields, map each to its own property, and make the builder write state.tooltip for tooltip.
limitations: Only the lengths were compared, not the exact strings. The value field (50%) matched in length.
verified_by: orchestrator package rerun (scenario-backed) or independent source verification (source-only); see VERIFICATION.md and verification-source-findings.md

title: GestureDetector onTap is not exposed as a semantic tap action
evidence: New at a19bf487: a GestureDetector with onTap around an 120x40 box has one Flutter node with the tap action; dispatching it calls onTap once (tap_calls 1 at frame 2). Incular has no node with an Activate action, so the tap cannot be dispatched (tap_calls 0). gestures.rs has no semantic contribution and the semantics role derivation (tree/semantics.rs:655-690) has no gesture arm.
impact: Any control built from a GestureDetector, with no Semantics or Button wrapper, is invisible to assistive technology and cannot be activated through it.
cause: Pointer callbacks are not mirrored into the semantic action set; only Button, Semantics and explicit widgets contribute callbacks.
fix_direction: Contribute tap and long-press actions from GestureDetector (and RawGestureDetector) to the semantic node, creating a generic node when needed, as Flutter's RenderSemanticsGestureHandler does.
limitations: Only tap was scenario-checked. Long press is covered by semantics-008, and drag and scroll gestures were not compared.
verified_by: orchestrator package rerun (scenario-backed) or independent source verification (source-only); see VERIFICATION.md and verification-source-findings.md

title: No long-press semantic action
evidence: Source reading at a19bf487: SemanticActionKind has Focus, Activate, SetText, SetSelection, Increment, Decrement, ScrollForward and ScrollBackward, and no long press. GestureDetector::on_long_press (gestures.rs:107-112) and the Semantics builder have no matching semantic callback. rg for LongPress and long_press in the semantics, widgets and accessibility crates finds nothing.
impact: Long-press-only actions, such as an item context menu, have no accessibility action, and assistive technology cannot trigger them.
cause: The portable action enum omits Flutter's SemanticsAction.longPress, and the gesture layer does not feed it.
fix_direction: Add a LongPress action kind, a Semantics on_long_press callback, and the GestureDetector mapping from semantics-007; route it to the native adapter.
limitations: Source-only. No frame scenario, because no Incular API exposes the action.
verified_by: orchestrator package rerun (scenario-backed) or independent source verification (source-only); see VERIFICATION.md and verification-source-findings.md

title: increasedValue and decreasedValue are not supported
evidence: Source reading at a19bf487: Flutter's SemanticsProperties has increasedValue and decreasedValue, and a debug assertion requires them when onIncrease or onDecrease is set with a non-empty value. Incular's on_increase and on_decrease only set the Increment and Decrement callbacks. SemanticNode has a single value field and no next/previous value. rg for increased_value and decreased finds nothing. The semantics__increase_decrease scenario checks only the action flags and callback counts, which match.
impact: Adjustable controls such as steppers or sliders cannot announce the value the next action will produce, so the user cannot predict an increment or decrement.
cause: The retained node model has no fields for the values after an increment or decrement.
fix_direction: Add optional increased and decreased value fields to the semantic state, set them from Semantics builders, and project them to the native adapter.
limitations: Source-only for the value fields. The action dispatch itself matched.
verified_by: orchestrator package rerun (scenario-backed) or independent source verification (source-only); see VERIFICATION.md and verification-source-findings.md

title: No semantic sort key or ordinal traversal order
evidence: Source reading at a19bf487: Flutter sorts sibling semantic nodes by SemanticsSortKey (OrdinalSortKey is the common form), so an app can reorder traversal without changing the widget tree. Incular's semantic child order is the widget child order (tree/semantics.rs:257-290) and no sort key appears in SemanticState, SemanticNode or the Semantics builder.
impact: Screen-reader order follows the widget tree. An app whose visual order differs from its reading order cannot correct it through semantics.
cause: The retained node model has no ordering key, and the semantics pass does not sort siblings.
fix_direction: Add an optional ordinal sort key to the semantic properties, and sort siblings within each parent by it (stable, with the widget order as the tiebreaker) as Flutter does.
limitations: Source-only. The ordering rule itself was not run against Flutter's sorted node output.
verified_by: orchestrator package rerun (scenario-backed) or independent source verification (source-only); see VERIFICATION.md and verification-source-findings.md
verification_note: Verification: IndexedSemantics is a collection index, not a sort key; the missing sort-key claim stands.

title: showOnScreen action is not available
evidence: Source reading at a19bf487: Flutter nodes can carry a showOnScreen handler that scrollable views use to bring an off-screen node into view, for example when assistive technology focuses it. SemanticActionKind has no ShowOnScreen kind and no Incular scroll view handles a reveal request; ScrollForward and ScrollBackward move by page only.
impact: Assistive technology cannot ask a scroll view to reveal an off-screen item before focusing it.
cause: The action set omits Flutter's showOnScreen, and the scroll views do not map a reveal request to a controller.
fix_direction: Add a ShowOnScreen action and route it through the scroll controller to reveal the target node's bounds.
limitations: Source-only. No scenario exercises reveal through the action path.
verified_by: orchestrator package rerun (scenario-backed) or independent source verification (source-only); see VERIFICATION.md and verification-source-findings.md

title: container and explicitChildNodes have no Incular equivalent
evidence: Source reading at a19bf487: Flutter's Semantics accepts container (force a separate node) and SemanticsConfiguration has explicitChildNodes (keep child nodes separate even under a merged parent). Incular's Semantics struct has neither flag, and every semantic node is decided by role (see semantics-004). Flutter's default non-container annotation merges into the nearest ancestor node, which has no Incular equivalent.
impact: Apps cannot choose whether a labelled wrapper is its own accessible node or merges into its parent, so grouping behavior differs from Flutter's default merge rules.
cause: The Incular builder has no container or explicit-child concept; node creation is role-driven.
fix_direction: Add container and explicit_child_nodes flags with Flutter's merge semantics, after the node creation rule in semantics-004 is fixed.
limitations: Source-only. The merge outcome for a non-container label was not run in Flutter.
verified_by: orchestrator package rerun (scenario-backed) or independent source verification (source-only); see VERIFICATION.md and verification-source-findings.md
verification_note: Verification: MergeSemantics exists; container and explicitChildNodes are what is missing.

title: CustomPaint has no per-painted-region semantics
evidence: Source reading at a19bf487: Flutter's CustomPainter can supply semanticsBuilder regions for painted content. rg for semantic in painting_effects/custom_paint.rs finds nothing; Incular's CustomPaint exposes no semantic region list. The only path is wrapping the whole painted area in Semantics.
impact: Individually meaningful painted parts (for example chart bars or custom controls) are not reachable to assistive technology unless the app wraps them in separate widgets.
cause: Painters have no semantic output in the Incular API.
fix_direction: Add an optional semantic region builder to the custom paint descriptor, producing child semantic nodes with bounds and labels.
limitations: Source-only; no custom-paint semantics scene exists in the frame harness.
verified_by: orchestrator package rerun (scenario-backed) or independent source verification (source-only); see VERIFICATION.md and verification-source-findings.md

title: TextSpan has no semanticsLabel
evidence: Source reading at a19bf487: Flutter's TextSpan can carry semanticsLabel, and InlineSpan combines it with children into semantics information. Incular's span model in crates/incular-text/src/spans.rs has no semantics field and no combine step, and rg for semanticsLabel or semantic_label across crates finds only unrelated image and menu labels.
impact: A span whose glyphs read badly (for example symbols or abbreviations) cannot be given a spoken replacement inside rich text.
cause: The span model carries no semantics information.
fix_direction: Add an optional semantics label to spans and combine span labels into the paragraph's node label, as Flutter's InlineSpan does.
limitations: Source-only; the combined label shape was not compared in Flutter.
verified_by: orchestrator package rerun (scenario-backed) or independent source verification (source-only); see VERIFICATION.md and verification-source-findings.md

title: SetText is advertised on an unfocused text field
evidence: New at resume: an unfocused EditableText. Flutter exposes no setText action (set_text_nodes 0), so the twin cannot dispatch it and the text stays empty (text_length 0). Incular advertises SetText because the field is enabled and not read-only (tree/semantics.rs:702-703), and dispatch sets the text to hello (text_length 5 at frame 2).
impact: Assistive technology can write into a field the user has not focused, which Flutter does not allow; the outcome differs in the same screen state.
cause: The Incular action gate checks enabled and read-only only, not focus.
fix_direction: Advertise SetText only when the field is focused and editable, matching Flutter's hasFocus && !readOnly rule.
limitations: Only the unfocused case was compared; the focused case (where Flutter does advertise SetText) was not run, because focusing a field from the twin needs a focus API that was not located.
verified_by: orchestrator package rerun (scenario-backed) or independent source verification (source-only); see VERIFICATION.md and verification-source-findings.md

title: Inline WidgetSpan carries no child widget, so inline widget semantics cannot exist
evidence: Source reading at a19bf487: Incular WidgetSpan has only id, size and alignment fields. Flutter's WidgetSpan holds a child widget whose semantics are placed in the paragraph at the placeholder's index. rg for PlaceholderSpan and placeholder semantics found no counterpart in the crates.
impact: A widget placed inline in rich text (an icon, a badge) cannot contribute its own accessibility node in reading order.
cause: The span model reserves a placeholder by id and size only, with no child widget or semantic index.
fix_direction: Give WidgetSpan an optional child widget that is laid out at the placeholder and contributes semantics at its index in the paragraph, as Flutter does.
limitations: Source-only. The app may place a widget at the placeholder id outside the span; that path was not traced to confirm it has no semantics.
verification_note: Duplicate of text-003 (WidgetSpan child replaced by plain text); same root cause.
